title: Always the latest build
prompt:
The download page always offers `builds/latest.tar`. Make it a symbolic link in `builds` that points to `pixel-raiders-1.1.tar` in the same folder, with a relative target, so the link keeps working when the whole `builds` folder moves.

Check it with `ls -l builds`.
hints: `ln -s TARGET LINK` creates a symbolic link; without `-s`, `ln` makes a hard link.
A relative target is resolved from the folder the link is in, not from where you run `ln`.
check:
if [ -L builds/latest.tar ]; then ok "builds/latest.tar is a symbolic link."
elif [ -e builds/latest.tar ]; then no "builds/latest.tar is a regular file, not a symbolic link. Delete it and use ln -s."; exit 1
else no "There is no builds/latest.tar yet."; exit 1; fi
t=$(readlink builds/latest.tar)
if [ "$t" = pixel-raiders-1.1.tar ] || [ "$t" = ./pixel-raiders-1.1.tar ]; then ok "It points to pixel-raiders-1.1.tar, relative to its folder."
elif [ "$t" = /home/mira/builds/pixel-raiders-1.1.tar ]; then no "It points to an absolute path, $t, which breaks when the folder moves."
else no "It points to “$t”, which isn’t pixel-raiders-1.1.tar in the same folder."; fi
if cmp -s builds/latest.tar builds/pixel-raiders-1.1.tar; then ok "Reading it gives the 1.1 build."; else no "Reading it doesn’t give the 1.1 build: the link is broken."; fi

title: A drop box like /tmp
prompt:
The studio wants a shared drop box in Mira’s home directory, `dropbox`, that works like `/tmp`: everyone may create files in it, but people may delete or rename only their own files.

Create it with the right permissions. Compare with `ls -ld /tmp`.
hints: Everyone needs read, write and execute on the folder: 777.
The sticky bit stops people deleting other people’s files in a folder everyone may write to. In `ls -l` it shows as a `t` in the last place.
check:
if [ -d dropbox ]; then ok "~/dropbox exists."; else no "There is no folder ~/dropbox yet."; exit 1; fi
m=$(stat -c %a dropbox)
if [ "$m" = 1777 ]; then ok "It is drwxrwxrwt (1777), like /tmp."
elif [ "$m" = 777 ]; then no "Everyone may write to it, but the sticky bit is missing, so anyone could delete anyone’s files."
else no "It is $(stat -c %a dropbox) ($(stat -c %A dropbox)), not drwxrwxrwt (1777)."; fi
